feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in leadership and consulting roles; this strengthens credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain alignment: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: business/user impact, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other constructions, and serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. lists without it). “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it will improve scanability and sharpen impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with a more direct verb-led phrase such as “leading enterprise platforms, governance, and content operations for.”
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience to increase credibility, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” here unless it is a priority target; the intro should emphasize web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI/search.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Delivers web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled search and content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” is more specific.
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in skills and experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; e.g., “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Refine for specificity and recency: “AI-enabled search & content discovery” is clearer than “content experiences.”
- Tighten and modernize wording:
  Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance & editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards & reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search & content discovery • Workflow automation & platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production & livestream operations
- Consider ordering by strongest differentiators first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, then communications and multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all three Topline Skills sections.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” also repeats content already covered in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with Work Experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Standardize wording and punctuation: use consistent verb tense, serial commas, and either “AI-enabled” or “AI-powered” throughout.
- Make outcomes more concrete where possible: e.g., “to improve policy-content discovery” could become “to speed discovery of legislative content” if accurate.
- Trim filler phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for ongoing expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles; consider framing them as “Selected projects” with sharper project-specific detail not stated elsewhere.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; keep it, as it adds range beyond the core experience bullets.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve cross-team coordination and reporting” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate technical delivery bullets: combine CMS development, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting into one concise execution bullet.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsites, AI search, and anniversary/campaign work are also detailed in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and outcome-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s channel-management details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Combine and streamline web modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: replace “reaching tens of thousands / serving thousands” with stronger metrics if available (open rates, engagement growth, campaign performance, production volume).
- Tighten operational bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building organizational capacity, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and quantify scope so it shows how this role set up the later director-level impact.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and organization-wide editorial coordination.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one outcome-oriented line: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in “Director of Digital Media”; keep this entry focused on execution, newsletters, video series and workflow building.
- “Weekly advocacy video update” also appears in the earlier NACo role and footer projects; vary wording or keep the stronger version in only one place.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less overlapping language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this skills block to scale shown in recent roles (10,000+ page platform, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than keeping it fully generic.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” overlap heavily with the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is somewhat redundant with recent work bullets on storytelling, campaign platforms, and editorial coordination.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences**
- Lead with Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-enabled search, since those are most supported by recent roles and projects.
- Replace “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” with a more impact-oriented label like **Web Platforms, Integrations & Automation**.
- If possible, tie this section to scale elsewhere in the CV by aligning wording with proven work: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills grouped and strategic, and leave full tool inventory to the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing across sections.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics capability and decision-making impact, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design and executive reporting” before listing platforms.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing higher-value, recent capabilities and using tighter, more senior phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with concise, senior-level terms: **Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual production operations**
- If you want more impact, swap one generic item for scope/outcome language: **In-house studio buildout and operations** or **Advocacy and event video production**
- Keep to 4 items max; avoid “video production and editing” if editing is not a differentiator versus leadership/operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; vary wording or remove it there.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so this skills block should stay abbreviated rather than repeat detail.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, this item should emphasize proficiency level or context rather than repeat a generic list.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualification to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization)** • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, group by strength: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep platform names only; avoid adding “CMS” or technical implementation terms here since those are covered elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This nearly repeats the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills entry; consider deleting one or making this version proficiency-based.
- Drupal is already heavily evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overexplaining it again here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Replace with: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows**
- Keep only tools you’ve actively used in recent roles/projects; if possible, swap one generic term for a higher-signal capability such as **custom front-end implementation** or **deployment automation**
- If space allows elsewhere, connect this stack to outcomes rather than listing versions (e.g., supported microsites, tracking deployments, or workflow automation)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing version numbers (**HTML5, CSS3**) unless older standards knowledge is relevant.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function and emphasize the strongest, most relevant tools first: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams; project tracking: Trello, Basecamp.”
- Consider trimming lower-value/general collaboration tools if space is tight; keep platforms that best support your recent systems/governance work.
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to make this more credible: “Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automation), Jira/Asana (editorial and project operations).”
- Use “Microsoft Teams” instead of “Teams” for consistency and searchability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams may feel too basic unless tied to operational use rather than simple familiarity.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to group by function and sharpen platform credibility: “Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope/level in parentheses to make it more meaningful: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise campaign orchestration), Higher Logic (member communications), Mailchimp (newsletter/campaign delivery)”
- Keep naming consistent and concise; “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys” is cleaner than using a slash.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency and depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating platform names there unless tied to a measurable outcome.
- “Engagement” may also overlap conceptually with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and recent NACo experience. Use it to sharpen technical specificity rather than restating broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard reporting**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** or **SEO/performance analysis** to make the skill more concrete and tool-aligned.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI/dashboard reporting** or **executive reporting** to better reflect business use.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity...**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially overlaps with **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one list or making this version more tool-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding generic terms here without added specificity.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads more like a summary than an achievement-focused role entry. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content production, with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and scope: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Split into 2 bullets and use action/result framing: one for website/workflow contributions, one for video/livestream production and informal supervision.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size of website refresh, frequency/audience of weekly videos, number of livestreams/events supported, growth in output, or team size.
- Sharpen phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” and “strengthening workflows” with specifics like “produced weekly advocacy videos and livestreams” and “standardized publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early-building the format.
- “Supporting the creation of the first in-house digital team” may echo later leadership entries; keep this role focused on implementation and early team formation.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, innovation support, and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer action/result, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content supporting program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Keep this entry shorter than recent roles—1 concise sentence or 2 bullets is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital media roles; avoid repeating generic production language.
- Since video/multimedia becomes a major theme later, use this entry to stress research/program support plus the podcast first-launch milestone.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but currently mixes software with capabilities, and it overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Tightening it into tool names plus one or two specific production systems will make it cleaner and less repetitive.

Suggested edit
- Rename or reframe as tools/platforms only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast editing/production”
- If you want stronger specificity, replace generic phrasing with actual platforms used, e.g., “vMix/OBS/StreamYard” or audio tools if accurate.
